# Stakeholder Analysis (Power/Interest Grid) 

![][image1]

| Quadrant  | Stakeholder Roles  | Engagement Strategy  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **High Power, High Interest** (Manage Closely)  | **Facility Manager:** Controls lot settings, dynamic pricing, and monitors dashboards. **Product Owner (Charlie D.):** Accountable for requirements and overall product value. **Project Manager (Ambar P.):** Responsible for schedule, budget, and risk mitigation. | Require daily engagement, direct involvement in scope approvals, and real-time visibility into project metrics and system dashboards.  |
| **High Power, Low Interest** (Keep Satisfied)  | **Traffic Planner / City Official:** External stakeholder using platform data for municipal routing. **Third-Party Payment / API Providers:** Providers of tokenized payments and mapping endpoints critical to platform function. | Provide aggregated heat map data and maintain strict adherence to API security rules to prevent credential exposure or service interruption.  |
| **Low Power, High Interest** (Keep Informed)  | **Driver / Vehicle Owner:** End-users searching, booking, and paying for spots. **Parking Lot Attendant:** Scans QR codes and manages live check-ins. **Enforcement Officer:** Validates license plates in real time. **Billing Specialist:** Manages partial refunds and daily settlements. | Ensure adequate training (e.g., Operator Training Mode), clear UI instructions, and timely system alerts regarding reservations or errors.  |
| **Low Power, Low Interest** (Monitor)  | **System Admin:** Manages databases, health, and user access. *(Note: Becomes High Interest during incidents)*  **General Public:** Non-app users impacted by city traffic routing. | Rely on automated PagerDuty alerts and synthetic checkout latency monitoring to ensure system stability without requiring constant manual intervention.  |
